questions.question: An optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$ with optimal solution $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is known for $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. The variable $x_{j'}$, which is nonbasic in $\mathcal{B}^*$, is removed from the program. What happens?
options: The basis stays feasible, but the reduced costs of the other nonbasic variables change and must be rechecked.
Nothing changes: $\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal, and $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ without its $j'$-th entry is still optimal.
The optimal value drops by the reduced cost $\bar{c}_{j'}$ of the removed variable, and the basic values adjust.
The program has to be solved again, since the constraint matrix $\boldsymbol{A}$ has lost one of its columns.

questions.question: An optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$ (basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$) of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ is known. A new variable $x_{j'}$ with price $c_{j'}$ and column $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$ is added. Which statement about the feasibility of $\mathcal{B}^*$ for the enlarged program is correct?
options: $\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible only when $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$; when $\bar{c}_{j'}<0$, the old solution violates a constraint.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible only when $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, so that no basic value turns negative.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible for every $c_{j'}$ and $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$, since $x_{j'}=0$ leaves $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ unchanged.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible for every $c_{j'}$ and $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$, since $x_{j'}$ joins the basis and $\boldsymbol{b}$ is unchanged.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, a new variable $x_{j'}$ gets the objective-row entry (reduced cost) $\bar{c}_{j'}=-c_{j'}+\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$. Which condition keeps $\mathcal{B}^*$ optimal, with $x_{j'}=0$?
options: $\bar{c}_{j'}\leq0$
$\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with $m$ constraints, the variable $x_{j'}$ is basic in the optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$ with value $x_{j'}^*>0$ in the optimal solution $\boldsymbol{x}^*$. The variable $x_{j'}$ is removed. What follows?
options: $\mathcal{B}^*$ keeps only $m-1$ columns, $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is no longer feasible, and the program is solved again.
$\boldsymbol{x}^*$ without its $j'$-th entry stays optimal, since removing a variable cannot raise the optimal value.
$x_{j'}$ becomes nonbasic, and only the sign of its reduced cost has to be checked, as for a new variable.
The optimal value becomes $Z^*-c_{j'}x_{j'}^*$, and the other basic variables keep their current values.

questions.question: A production plan $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ (row $i$ is resource $i$) has optimal shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*$. A new product uses $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$ per unit and sells at $c_{j'}$. What does the number $\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$ measure?
options: The profit that one unit of the new product earns once it is taken into the optimal plan.
The amounts of the resources that are still unused after one unit of the new product is made.
The value, at the current shadow prices, of the resources that one unit of the new product uses.
The change in the basic variables of the current plan when one unit of the new product is made.

questions.question: An optimal plan of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ with three resource constraints has shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(2,0,5)^{\top}$. Buying extra units of resource $3$ at $4$ per unit is a new variable $x_7$ with $c_7=-4$ and $\boldsymbol{A}_7=(0,0,-1)^{\top}$: each unit bought relaxes the third constraint by one. What is $\bar{c}_7=-c_7+\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}\boldsymbol{A}_7$?

An optimal plan of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(\tfrac{1}{2},3,0)^{\top}$ for its three resources. A new product uses $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}=(4,1,5)^{\top}$ per unit and sells at $c_{j'}$. For which prices does the current optimal basis stay optimal?
options: Exactly when $c_{j'}\geq5$
Exactly when $c_{j'}\leq\tfrac{11}{2}$
Exactly when $c_{j'}\leq\tfrac{7}{2}$
Exactly when $c_{j'}\leq5$

questions.question: An optimal basis of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has basic variables $x_1=3$, $x_3=0$, $s_1=2$ and nonbasic variables $x_2$, $s_2$, $s_3$. One of $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$ is removed at a time. Which removals force the linear program to be solved again?
options: Removing $x_1$ or removing $x_3$, as both of them are basic.
Only removing $x_1$, the basic variable with a positive value.
Removing any one of $x_1$, $x_2$ or $x_3$, as a column is lost.
No removal, since removing a variable cannot raise $Z^*$.

questions.question: A final tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form has basic variables $(x_2,s_2)$ and $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}\tfrac{1}{2}&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$. A new variable $x_5$ with column $\boldsymbol{A}_5=(4,6)^{\top}$ is added. Which column is written into the tableau under $x_5$, in the rows of $x_2$ and $s_2$?

In an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, the nonbasic product $x_2$ with price $c_2=4$ has objective-row entry (reduced cost) $\bar{c}_2=3$. A new product $x_6$ uses exactly the same resources per unit, $\boldsymbol{A}_6=\boldsymbol{A}_2$, and sells at $c_6=9$. What is its objective-row entry $\bar{c}_6=-c_6+\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}\boldsymbol{A}_6$?

A new variable $x_{j'}$ with column $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$ is added to $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. Its reduced cost is negative, so it enters the final tableau of the optimal basis (basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$). Which column does the ratio test for $x_{j'}$ use, and why?
options: $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$, as the tableau rows are the constraints multiplied by $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$.
$\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$, as the constraints of the program are unchanged when a variable is added.
A unit vector, as the new variable gets a new row of its own in the final tableau.
$\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$, as $x_{j'}$ is nonbasic and $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ acts only on the basic columns.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$ and nondegenerate optimal solution $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ of value $Z^*$, a new variable $x_{j'}$ gets the objective-row entry (reduced cost) $\bar{c}_{j'}=-c_{j'}+\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}=0$. Which statement about the enlarged program is correct?
options: $\mathcal{B}^*$ is no longer optimal, as $x_{j'}$ is an entering candidate that raises $Z$.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal, and letting $x_{j'}$ enter gives another solution of value $Z^*$.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal, and $x_{j'}$ is $0$ in every optimal solution of the enlarged program.
$\boldsymbol{x}^*$ is no longer feasible, as a variable with reduced cost $0$ has to be basic.

questions.question: A linear program $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has finite optimal value $Z^*$. One variable is added or one variable is removed, with the constraints otherwise unchanged. Which statement about the new optimal value is correct?
options: Adding a variable with price $c_{j'}>0$ always raises the optimal value above $Z^*$.
Removing a basic variable always lowers the optimal value strictly below $Z^*$.
Removing a variable never changes the optimal value, as the others take over its role.
Adding a variable cannot lower it, and removing a variable cannot raise it.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ has $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}=(2,3,0)^{\top}$ and $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\tfrac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}3&-1&0\\-1&1&0\\-5&1&2\end{pmatrix}$. A product $x_3$ with $c_3=3$, $\boldsymbol{A}_3=(2,1,3)^{\top}$ is added. What is its reduced cost $\bar{c}_3$ (objective-row entry)?

A product $x_7$ with negative reduced cost is added to an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$. Its column is $\boldsymbol{A}_7=(1,2,1)^{\top}$ and its updated column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_7=(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{3}{2},-1)^{\top}$, in the rows of the basic variables $x_2=4$, $s_1=3$, $x_1=6$. Which variable leaves, and what value does $x_7$ get?
options: $s_1$ leaves, and $x_7=2$.
$s_1$ leaves, and $x_7=\tfrac{3}{2}$.
$x_2$ leaves, and $x_7=8$.
$s_1$ leaves, and $x_7=\tfrac{9}{2}$.

questions.question: An optimal plan of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has $Z^*=40$ and shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(2,1)^{\top}$. A product $x_8$ with $\boldsymbol{A}_8=(1,3)^{\top}$ and $c_8=8$ is added; the ratio test lets it enter at $x_8=4$. What is $Z$ after this simplex iteration?

For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}^*$, a variable $x_{j'}$ with price $c_{j'}$ and column $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$ is added. How does the dual change, and what does $\bar{c}_{j'}=-c_{j'}+\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}\geq0$ say?
options: A new dual variable $y_{m+1}\geq0$ appears, and $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$ says that $y_{m+1}=0$ at the dual optimum.
The dual gains $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq c_{j'}$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$ says that $\boldsymbol{y}^*$ violates this constraint.
The dual objective becomes $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}+c_{j'}$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$ says its optimal value is unchanged.
The dual gains $\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq c_{j'}$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$ says that $\boldsymbol{y}^*$ still satisfies this constraint.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, optimal solution $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ and value $Z^*$, a new variable $x_{j'}$ gets the objective-row entry (reduced cost) $\bar{c}_{j'}<0$, and its updated column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$ has a positive entry. Which statement about what $\bar{c}_{j'}<0$ implies is correct?
options: It implies that the enlarged program has an optimal value larger than $Z^*$.
It implies that $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ with $x_{j'}=0$ is no longer a feasible solution.
It implies that $\mathcal{B}^*$ fails the optimality test of the enlarged program.
It implies that the enlarged program is unbounded in the direction of $x_{j'}$.

questions.question: $\max Z=2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $x_1+3x_2\leq12$, $2x_1+x_2\leq10$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ with $x_1=x_2=3$, $s_3=1$, $Z^*=15$. A bundle $x_3$ uses the resources of one unit of each product, $\boldsymbol{A}_3=(2,4,3)^{\top}$, and sells at $c_3=7$. What value of $Z$ does one simplex iteration with $x_3$ entering reach?

$\max Z=x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $x_1+3x_2\leq12$, $2x_1+x_2\leq10$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ with $x_1^*=x_2^*=3$, $s_3^*=1$ and $Z^*=12$. The variable $x_1$ is removed. Which statement about the optimal value of the remaining program is correct?
options: It drops to $9$, since the contribution $c_1x_1^*=3$ of $x_1$ is lost.
It stays $12$, since $x_2$ can rise to $4$ and make up for the whole loss.
It drops below $12$, since a basic variable with a positive value is removed.
It stays $12$, since $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ without its entry $x_1^*$ is still optimal.
